'''Jaroslav Nešetřil''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈjaroslaf ˈnɛʃɛtr̝̊ɪl}}; born 13 March 1946) is a [[Czechs|Czech]] [[mathematician]]. His research areas include [[combinatorics]] (structural combinatorics, [[Ramsey theory]]), [[graph theory]] (coloring problems, sparse structures), [[algebra]] (representation of structures, [[category theory|categories]], [[graph homomorphism|homomorphisms]]), [[Partially ordered sets|posets]] (diagram and [[Order dimension|dimension]] problems), [[computer science]] ([[Computational complexity theory|complexity]], [[P = NP problem|NP-completeness]]). He works at [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]].

==Education and career==
Nešetřil received his [[Ph.D.]] from Charles University in 1973 under the supervision of Aleš Pultr and [[Gert Sabidussi]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=80983}}</ref> He is responsible for more than 300 publications.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~nesetril/pdf/biblio_published.pdf|title=List of publications of Jaroslav Nešetřil|date=n.d.|access-date=29 August 2023}}</ref> Since 2006, he is chairman of the Committee of Mathematics of Czech Republic (the Czech partner of [[International Mathematical Union|IMU]]).

Jaroslav Nešetřil is Editor in Chief of ''Computer Science Review''<ref>[http://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaleditorialboard.cws_home/710138/editorialboard Editorial Board], Computer Science Review, [[Elsevier]]. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref> and ''INTEGERS: the Electronic Journal of Combinatorial Number Theory''.<ref>[http://www.integers-ejcnt.org/edboard.html Editorial Board], INTEGERS: the Electronic Journal of Combinatorial Number Theory. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref>
He is also honorary editor of ''Electronic Journal of Graph Theory and Applications''.<ref>[http://ejgta.org/index.php/ejgta/about/editorialTeam Editorial Team], Electronic Journal of Graph Theory and Applications. Accessed 14 June 2013</ref> Since 2008, Jaroslav Nešetřil belongs to the Advisory Board of the [[Academia Sinica]].<ref>[http://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/www/people/advisor_e.jsp Advisory Board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719003715/http://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/www/people/advisor_e.jsp |date=2011-07-19}}, Academia Sinica. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref>

==Awards and honors==
He was awarded the state prize (1985 jointly with [[Vojtěch Rödl]]) for a collection of papers in Ramsey theory. The book ''Sparsity - Graphs, Structures, and Algorithms'' he co-authored with [[Patrice Ossona de Mendez]] was included in [[ACM Computing Reviews]]
list of ''Notable Books and Articles of 2012''.<ref>[http://www.computingreviews.com/recommend/bestof/notableitems_2012.cfm ACM Computing Reviews - Notable Computing Books and Articles of 2012], ACM Computing Reviews website. Accessed 29 June 2013</ref>

Nešetřil is a corresponding member of the German Academy of Sciences since 1996 and has been declared Doctor Honoris Causa of the University of Alaska ([[Fairbanks]]) in 2002. He has also been declared Doctor Honoris Causa of the [[University of Bordeaux 1]] in 2009; the speech he made in French at this occasion attracted a great deal of attention.<ref>"Échos de Talence", [[Sud-Ouest (newspaper)|Sud Ouest]]. 2009, September 11th</ref> He received in 2010 the [[State decorations of the Czech Republic#The Medal of Merit|Medal of Merit of Czech Republic]]<ref>[http://www.hrad.cz/en/czech-republic/state-decorations/medal-of-merit/list.shtml List of the recipients of the Medal of Merit], Prague Castle Website. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref> and the Gold medal of Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Charles University in 2011. In 2012, he has been elected to the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>[http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Nesetril_Jaroslav Jaroslav Nešetřil's page on Academia Europaea], Academia Europaea website. Accessed 12 November 2012</ref> Also, he has been elected honorary member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>[http://mta.hu/articles/new-members-of-the-hungarian-academy-of-sciences-131864/ New members of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903115610/http://mta.hu/articles/new-members-of-the-hungarian-academy-of-sciences-131864/ |date=2014-09-03 }}, Website of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. Accessed 11 May 2013</ref>

He was an invited speaker of the [[European Congress of Mathematics]], in [[Amsterdam]], 2008,<ref>[http://www.5ecm.nl/program Program] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100801034412/http://www.5ecm.nl/program |date=2010-08-01}}, ECM 2008. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref> and invited speaker (by both the Logic and Foundations and Combinatorics sections) at the Combinatorics session of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Hyderabad]], 2010.<ref>[http://www.icm2010.org.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers Invited Speakers for ICM2010] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717191917/http://www.icm2010.org.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers |date=2011-07-17 }}, ICM 2010 Website. Accessed 29 January 2011</ref>

In 2018, on the occasion of the 670th anniversary of the establishment of Charles University, Nešetřil has received from the rector of Charles university the [[Donatio Universitatis Carolinae]] prize “for his contribution to mathematics and for his leading role in establishing a world-renowned group in discrete mathematics at Charles University”.<ref>[https://www.mff.cuni.cz/verejnost/konalo-se/2018-04-nesetril/ Donatio Universitatis Carolinae pro prof. Nešetřila]</ref>

Together with [[Patrice Ossona de Mendez]], he received the 2025 [[Nerode Prize]] for his work on Sparsity for the papers
''Grad and classes with bounded expansion I. Decompositions'', ''Grad and classes with bounded expansion II. Algorithmic aspects'', ''First order properties on nowhere dense structures'',  and ''On nowhere dense graphs''.<ref>{{citation|url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/3009-eatcs-ipec-nerode-prize-2025|title=EATCS-IPEC Nerode Prize 2025|work=EATCS |publisher=[[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]]|accessdate=2025-09-26}}.</ref>
